question: Which option is correct when converting 27°C to the Kelvin scale?
solution:
**Concept**

 
• Temperature can be measured in different scales such as Celsius (°C), Kelvin (K), and Fahrenheit (°F).
 
• The Kelvin scale is the SI unit of temperature and is also known as the absolute temperature scale.
 
• To convert from the Celsius scale to the Kelvin scale, a constant value is added to the Celsius temperature because the zero point of the Kelvin scale (absolute zero) is -273.15^circ {C}.
